Old graphics cards learn new tricks

Written by A. Writer on 3 October
Over the past year, a driver developer has made several improvements to the kernel driver for old graphics cards, so that they handle games and other tasks better. This week, at a conference in a large city, she presented this work, which she began as an exercise.

She has become a legend for owners of old graphics cards, moving them from the legacy driver to the modern one, which unlocks a newer graphics API, better performance, and better functionality overall. In the process, she fixed defects in the display code and in the power management of these cards.


For those wishing to hear the whole story, a recording of the talk is available, along with the slides, and the talk also covers how to get involved in driver development in Toronto and elsewhere.
